segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for November 18, 2026.
Today we cover new regulations for autonomous vehicles, major funding for data sharing, and exciting developments in AI-powered robotics.
From The Robot Report, "California DMV bars Waymo AVs from operating on the state’s freeways".
This segment details the California Department of Motor Vehicles' action to restrict Waymo autonomous vehicles from operating on state freeways following safety concerns.
The DMV determined that freeway operations presented an imminent hazard due to Waymo vehicles entering active construction closures and interacting with law enforcement personnel.
This restriction was implemented because of specific incidents where Waymo vehicles entered areas under construction and engaged with law enforcement activity.
Waymo indicated that the ban is limited to freeways, maintaining service on city streets.
The company stated that the restriction remains in place pending demonstration of corrective actions addressing these identified deficiencies.
The industry will observe the implementation of these corrective measures by Waymo to determine future operational parameters.
From TechCrunch - Robotics, India’s Humyn Labs raises forty-seven million dollars in Series A funding to supply real-world data for training U.S. robotics and artificial intelligence companies.
The company utilizes two-camera hardware to record and process footage of individuals performing routine tasks across more than twenty nations.
This process involves collecting data concerning actions, hand movements, and object interactions to construct usable sets for artificial intelligence training.
Revenue generation primarily stems from U.S. clientele, including robotics firms and AI research laboratories.
The initiative brings into focus critical considerations regarding privacy and consent in large-scale data collection practices.
This development signals an emerging trend in the provision of cross-national, real-world data essential for advancing robotics and AI model development.
From TechCrunch - Robotics, Genesis AI raises five hundred million dollars in a Series A round to advance its glove-wearing robot technology.
The company has demonstrated complex manipulation skills through its physical AI model operating robotic arms.
Genesis AI gathers force data using sensor-enabled gloves worn by workers to train its model.
The company focuses on vertical integration, developing its own data, AI model, and humanoid robot design.
The primary bottleneck for Genesis is achieving industrial-grade hardware and sufficient real-world data for generalized robotic intelligence.
This development signals increased investment in tactile sensing and embodied AI systems within the robotics sector.
Future developments will focus on overcoming hardware limitations to advance generalized robotic intelligence.
From Robotics & Automation News, THG Fulfil has doubled the AutoStore capacity at its Warrington warehouse.

This development reflects an expansion to two hundred forty thousand bins, increasing the AutoStore storage capacity at the Omega facility to eight point four million units through the deployment of additional robots and carousel ports.

This automated infrastructure directly addresses retailer concerns regarding increasing labor costs and customer satisfaction by enabling brands to manage hypergrowth and absorb volume spikes while maintaining operational speed and accuracy.
THG Fulfil operates as both a distributor and an end-user of AutoStore technology globally.
This expansion demonstrates the growing integration of advanced automation solutions within large-scale logistics operations.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries expand Spot operations and prepare to test Atlas humanoid".
This report details the expansion of Spot deployments for asset management at GlobalFoundries sites and the upcoming testing of the Atlas humanoid robot.
Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries are expanding Spot deployments for autonomous asset management across GlobalFoundries' semiconductor fabrication sites in multiple locations.
This collaboration involves Spot already helping GlobalFoundries shift to predictive maintenance by collecting data across inspection points in their fabrication plants.
Furthermore, GlobalFoundries will be the first non-automotive customer to begin testing the Atlas humanoid robot as part of an early adopter program.
Testing of Atlas at the GlobalFoundries facilities is scheduled to commence in early 2027 to evaluate potential use cases and integration requirements.
This development signals a progression in applying advanced robotics and artificial intelligence to complex manufacturing environments globally.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Groundworks 2026 calls for faster adoption of construction robotics in UK".
This report details the discussions held at Groundworks 2026 regarding the deployment of construction robotics on active sites to address the labor shortage.
The event focused on the necessity of early planning for suitable tasks, establishing viable supply chains, and building client confidence through demonstrated project evidence.

Speakers presented methodologies for how automation can enhance productivity and support teams while factoring in site-specific conditions, emphasizing the need to test robotics against dynamic site changes and concentrate on task-specific solutions.
This gathering included industry stakeholders, developers, investors, and policymakers to discuss the commercial and practical integration of these technologies.
Wider adoption depends on ongoing testing and task-focused implementation strategies.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS Wiki Content Migration Effort".

This story details an initiative to migrate documentation from the archived ROS wiki into README.md files for ROS packages, aiming to make this valuable documentation accessible within GitHub repositories.
A process was initiated to extract package-specific content, convert it to Markdown, and aggregate it into proposed READMEs through a pipeline.
This effort requires manual review and filtering of the content to ensure quality before initiating pull requests against the noetic branch.
The bulk migration seeks to preserve essential ROS wiki information directly within the codebase.
This migration effort contributes to improved accessibility of foundational ROS knowledge within the development ecosystem.
From The Robot Report, "Learn how AI is changing supply chain robotics".
This report details how artificial intelligence is transforming supply chain robotics to address labor shortages, improve efficiency, and build resilience.
Warehouse automation, autonomous mobile robots, and AI-powered inventory management represent current technologies in this transformation.
Artificial intelligence facilitates predictive analytics, demand forecasting, and dynamic routing to optimize robot performance within these systems.
Integrating these technologies allows for end-to-end supply chain optimization that adapts to shifting demand and supports high-volume production.
These advancements result in higher quality, reduced downtime, and cost optimization for manufacturers.
The integration of these systems signals a significant shift in industrial operations.
Further development in this area will continue to redefine logistics and manufacturing landscapes.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Wildfire Tech is Automating Everything but the Hose".
This report details the integration of artificial intelligence, aerial coordination, and autonomous suppression launchers into wildfire response efforts, demonstrating progress in automation.
The response strategy involves establishing detection and coordination layers utilizing AI for early detection and aerial management.
Autonomous suppression launchers are being deployed for targeted application, while electric pumps are being trialed to provide a controllable platform for future automation.
However, the physical act of moving water across unstructured terrain remains a significant challenge resistant to full autonomy.
The current setup establishes advanced detection and coordination systems while acknowledging that physical application constitutes the final, necessary step in suppression operations.
This indicates a focus on layered technological integration as the immediate bottleneck for complete autonomous response systems.
From RoboPapers, "Ep#117: Residual Modeling Closes the Regression and Generative Policy Gap in Robot Learning"
reports on a method that addresses a performance discrepancy in robot learning from demonstrations.

The research demonstrates that generative policies often surpass direct action regression methods, and this gap is primarily linked to mismatches in loss functions arising from state-dependent action residuals and heavy-tailed data distributions.
The authors introduced HT-Policies, a framework designed to learn input-dependent residual scales and incorporate a Student-t residual model to manage the effect of heavy tails in the data.
These HT-Policies achieved performance comparable to generative baselines while exhibiting accelerated training and inference times.
Accounting for the distribution and scale of the action residuals is shown to be a critical factor for effective policy optimization in robot learning systems.
This research indicates a pathway toward more robust and efficient policy optimization in embodied AI.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Spirit v1.5!".
This segment reports on the release of an open-source robot foundation model and its initial performance metrics.
The model, Spirit v1.5, was developed by Spirit AI and released on January 12, 2026, within the vision-language-action category for robotics.
The software is designed for integration into robotic systems rather than a physical robot and currently scores a Humanoid Guide Brain of five out of ten.
Training for the model emphasized collecting varied data derived from less scripted operator activity to increase data diversity, which facilitated faster learning.
The model achieved the first place ranking on RoboChallenge, an evaluation benchmark utilizing real robots, demonstrating its demonstrated capability.
Spirit AI made both the model and the corresponding code publicly available to encourage further development in home robot foundations.
This release indicates a step forward in making advanced robotics models accessible for broader research and development.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Quanta X1 Pro!".
This report details the introduction of a new wheeled, humanoid research platform developed by X Square Robot, emphasizing mobile manipulation over legged movement.
The platform measures one hundred sixty-nine centimeters tall and weighs eighty kilograms, featuring two arms and extensive camera arrays for sensing capabilities.
This system utilizes wheeled mobility to perform tasks such as sorting goods, assembling products, and obstacle avoidance, incorporating onboard computing, AI models, and ROS2 support.
Current assessment indicates a developing overall skill score of four out of ten, with enhanced manipulation capabilities noted over navigation skills.
This development signals further progress in mobile robotics application for research and industry.
From Robotics & Automation News, ClearSpace moves closer to launch of European space debris removal mission.

This report details an agreement made to provide navigation and capture technologies for the European Space Agency’s ClearSpace-1 mission, which seeks to demonstrate the safe capture and removal of an unprepared object from Earth orbit.
ClearSpace will develop the necessary technologies to approach, navigate, and capture objects in orbit, targeting the Proba-1 satellite to prove robotic capture capability for space debris removal.
This collaboration involves ClearSpace and OHB System AG supplying the requisite navigation and capture systems for the mission.
Additionally, ClearSpace is advancing commercial in-orbit servicing capabilities through other European space programs.
This development signals advancements in robotic manipulation techniques applicable to future space infrastructure and debris mitigation efforts.
